predecessors.note: The Mértola page dates the independence 1031, the Taifa page 1033 (its infobox c. 1037).

land.text: Mértola, 'finally conquered by the Almohad Caliphate' in 1151; Almohad 1151-1250

rulers.note: The page lists him as ruler 1033-1044 and as the Seville ruler who took Mértola in 1044; the Mértola dynasty before 1044 is not named.

correction.text: Mértola and its district: southeastern Portugal, the page gives no towns beyond the capital

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Mértola row (its nearest are Taifa of Santa Maria do Algarve 1018-1055, Taifa of Silves 1040-1168 and Taifa of Badajoz). A 20 km circle (about 1,260 km2) matches the municipality area of 1,292.87 km2 given on the Mértola page, which that page does not tie to the Islamic period.

correction.text: Mértola and its district under Ibn Qasi, 'seat of an independent state' 1144-1150 (Mértola page), 1144-1151 (Taifa page)

keyframe_review.note: Gap in 1145 (Badajoz). The Ibn Qasi page says his state was centred on Silves, which the Taifa of Silves dossier covers.

ledger.note: 1033: Mértola becomes an independent taifa. 'It existed during three distinct periods: from 1033 to 1044, from 1144 to 1145, and from 1146 to 1151'; infobox 'Downfall of Caliphate of Córdoba: 1033' and 'c. 1037'. The Mértola page: 'After the fall of the Caliphate of Córdoba, in 1031, Mértola became an independent taifa state.'

1044: Seville takes Mértola. 'From 1044 until 1091 it was under the forcible control of the Taifa of Seville, by Abbad II al-Mu'tadid'; the Mértola page: 'conquered by the taifa of Seville in 1044-1045'.

1144: Mértola is independent again under Ibn Qasi, a mystic and military leader who 'fought the power of the Almoravides' (Mértola page: 'Between 1144 and 1150 the town was again seat of an independent state led by Ibn Qasi'). Almoravid rule 1091-1144 on the Taifa page.
1145: 'Badajoz period: 1145-1146' on the Taifa page; the page does not say how it passed.
1146: Ibn Qasi is 'restored 1146-1151' (Taifa page ruler list).

1151: 'Its short-lived history ended in 1151, when it was finally conquered by the Almohad Caliphate' (Almohad 1151-1250); Ibn Qasi died in 1151 (Ibn Qasi page). The Mértola page says only that 'the independence of the region was soon ended by an invading Almohad army' (no year).
1151: the Taifa of Mértola ends; the Portuguese took the town in 1238.

wars.name: Revolt of Ibn Qasi
wars.outcome: Ibn Qasi's followers (murid revolt) made Mértola and Silves independent of the Almoravids in 1144; he rebelled with Portuguese help against the Almohads and was beheaded by his own followers in 1151.
wars.note: The Ibn Qasi page gives no year for the revolt and does not mention Mértola; the Mértola page gives 1144-1150 for the independent state.

certainty.note: The pages name Mértola only; the 20 km circle echoes the modern municipality's area.

sources.title: Taifa of Mértola
sources.note: Three periods (1033-1044, 1144-1145, 1146-1151), Seville 1044-1091, Almoravids 1091-1144, Badajoz 1145-1146, Almohads 1151-1250; no founder, no territory.

sources.title: Mértola
sources.note: Independent taifa from 1031; Seville 1044-1045; Ibn Qasi's state 1144-1150; Sancho II 1238; municipality 1,292.87 km2.

sources.title: Ibn Qasi
sources.note: Revolt centred on Silves; against Almoravids then Almohads; beheaded 1151; no Mértola.

notes: Written for eu-12-x (asked for by eu-12-h as taifa-of-mertola, 1044-45); three pages. Cliopatria has no row. The founding year differs by page (1031 Mértola, 1033 Taifa, c. 1037 infobox); the Seville conquest is 1044 (Taifa) or 1044-1045 (Mértola); the Ibn Qasi state is 1144-1145 and 1146-1151 (Taifa) or 1144-1150 (Mértola). Not settled: who ruled Mértola 1033-1044 (the Taifa page lists Abbad II al-Mu'tadid, the Seville ruler, for the same years); the territory beyond the town; what the Taifa of Silves dossier says of Ibn Qasi (his city-state at Silves). Gazetteer name needed: Mértola (place, Portugal).
